entities.summary:
Girolamo Genga (1480-1551) was an Italian painter and architect of the late Renaissance, Mannerist style.

Born in Urbino, Italy, Genga studied under renowned artists such as Baldassare Peruzzi and Francesco Melzi, eventually becoming a prominent figure in the Mannerist movement.

His notable works include the frescoes in the Vatican's Stanze di Raffaello, which showcase his mastery of intricate composition and vivid color palette.

Genga's legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including Raphael and Michelangelo, who were heavily influenced by his work.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Genga's frescoes in the Vatican continue to inspire artists and art historians to this day, offering a glimpse into the creative genius of a true Renaissance master.
